industry.structure: Indian lead-acid batteries are a duopoly in the organised market: Exide and Amara Raja (ARE&M) lead auto OEM and replacement; Exide leads industrial (railways, traction, power, submarine, UPS) except telecom. The replacement channel (B2C) is ~65-70% of Exide's business (AR FY26).
industry.demand: Auto OEM grew ~25% YoY for three straight quarters after the GST cut (28% to 18% on batteries and vehicles, effective 22-Sep-2025); replacement demand follows OEM fitments 2.5-3 years later (Q1FY27 call). Home inverters/UPS ~15-25% of revenue by season; solar crossed Rs1,000 cr in FY26 (PM Surya Ghar rooftop scheme).
industry.threat: Lithium-ion is taking telecom and e-rickshaw batteries now and 2W/3W/4W EV batteries as EVs grow. India's EV cell demand ~20-25 GWh today (CEO, Q1FY27 call), 140-150 GWh by 2030 (BCG, Q1FY27 deck), still largely imported from China.
industry.costs: Lead, acid (sulphur) and plastics are ~95-96% of the bill of materials (Q4FY26 call). Lead is bought at import parity: a weaker rupee offsets lower LME prices. Sulphur rose from ~Rs15 to Rs75/kg over FY26 (Q4FY26 call). OEM and institutional contracts carry lead-price formulas; trade prices are raised in steps (Jan, Mar, Apr-2026, ~5-6% plus ~3%; Q1FY27 +4-6% YoY).

named: Chloride Eastern Ltd, UK (promoter; holding company by de facto control)
ownership.src: Screener.in shareholding (Jun-2026 categories); AR FY26 note 15 (holders above 5% at 31-Mar-2026: Chloride Eastern 39.10 cr shares, LIC 4.48 cr shares)
ownership.pledge: Pledge status not shown in our Jun-2026 source (Screener categories); the promoter is a single UK holding company.

moat.brand: Exide is the best-known battery brand in India; 120,000+ network touchpoints, 1,600+ Exide Care outlets, doorstep 'Batmobile' service (Q1FY27 deck).
moat.scale: 16 plants including 3 lead-recycling plants of Chloride Metals (captive recycled lead ~79% of lead used, AR FY26).
moat.oem: 75+ OEMs; 100% share of business on key new models of large OEMs (Q1FY27 deck).
moat.weakness: Lead-acid is a commodity-cost business with a duopoly rival of similar scale; margins are 10.7-12.3% (FY22-26), below the 13-15% of FY15-21. Lithium is a different technology where Exide has no edge in cells, relies on a Chinese technology partner (SVOLT) and imported materials, and is not in the ACC PLI scheme.

critiques: Returns: standalone ROE fell from 13-15% (FY17-19) to 8-9% (FY23-26) because ~Rs10,000 cr of equity sits in the HDFC Life stake and EESL, which earn little or nothing (MOFSL: ROE 7.6% in FY26).
Capital allocation: Rs4,902 cr already put into EESL with no revenue yet from cells; Rs1,400 cr more approved for FY27 and Phase 2 (6 to 12 GWh) 'might exceed' earlier plans (Q1FY27 call).
MOFSL: lithium-ion is a low-margin business globally and is likely to dilute returns even if it succeeds.
Kotak: profitability and return ratios under pressure from heavy lithium capex.

governance.board: 9 directors, 4 independent (44%); Chairman Sridhar Gorthi (independent); Vice-Chairman Rajan B Raheja (non-executive, non-independent); MD & CEO Avik Roy (since Jan-2019 at Exide); Director-Finance & CFO Manoj Agarwal (since Feb-2023); Executive Director Pravin Saraf also MD & CEO of EESL (AR FY26).
governance.auditor: B S R & Co. LLP (AR FY26).
governance.relatedParty: Corporate guarantees for EESL borrowings (guarantee commission Rs5.6 cr in FY26, AR FY26 note 26); Chloride Metals supplies recycled lead to Exide.

gaps: EESL forecasts: no company guidance and no broker publishes EESL P&L forecasts; our losses to breakeven are GAM estimates (assumptions.build.eesl).
Business-line revenue: only ballpark figures exist (auto ~50-53%, home UPS ~Rs2,300 cr, solar >Rs1,000 cr, exports Rs915 cr, telecom ~2-3%); the FY26 split is a GAM approximation.
Citi, Nomura, J.P. Morgan and Kotak: valuation method and multiple not available; dates taken from aggregators (4-Aug-2026, the first trading day after the results call).
Named shareholders above 1% for Jun-2026 were not retrieved; LIC's 5.27% is from the Mar-2026 annual report.
ACC-PLI-style subsidy amounts EESL may receive are 'not in public domain' (CEO, Q1FY27 call).
Hyundai-Kia co-investment line: no size or timing disclosed (non-binding MoU).
conflicts: Insurance holding: Exide's listed insurance stake is HDFC Life (8,70,22,222 shares received on 1-Jan-2022 for Exide Life, AR FY23 note 54; unchanged at Mar-2026, AR FY26 note 4). It holds no ICICI Prudential Life shares; its only ICICI Prudential holding is a liquid mutual fund (Rs59 cr, AR FY26 note 9).
HDFC Life's Jun-2026 shareholding filing shows Exide at 4.01% (official PDF snippet) vs 4.04% on aggregators; the share count (8,70,22,222) is the same in both.
EBITDA: Screener standalone FY26 Rs1,946 cr vs the company's operating profit Rs1,943 cr (10-year table); Q1FY27 margin 12.3% (Screener) vs 12.4% (company). We use Screener's basis in the model.
MOFSL describes Q1FY27 cell supplies as 'commercial customer deliveries'; the company calls them customer samples, with revenue 'during FY27'.
